title: Transport of ordinary units and sections between the two sites
statement:
Let $f:Y\to X$ be a quasi-compact, quasi-separated scheme morphism and $\Lambda$ a finite discrete commutative ring. Work in the small-etale and small-pro-etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] with exact comparison $C_T=\nu_T^*$ [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $L$ be an etale sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $X$, in degree zero. Put $l=f_{\mathrm{et}}^{-1}$, $r=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-pbc-direct-image] and $P=Lf_{\mathrm{proet}}^*$, $s=Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Write $\eta^e,\eta^p$ for the units, $a:C_Yl\cong PC_X$ for the canonical pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback], and $b:C_Xr\to sC_Y$ for the counit-normalized comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Then
$$\eta^p_{C_XL}=s(a_L)\circ b_{lL}\circ C_X(\eta^e_L).$$
If $\eta^e_L:L\to rlL$ is invertible, the pro-etale unit $\eta^p_{C_XL}$ is invertible, and the ordinary pullback maps
$$R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{et}},L)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{et}},lL),\qquad R\Gamma(X_{\mathrm{proet}},C_XL)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},PC_XL)$$
are isomorphisms of derived $\Lambda$-modules. Under $a_L$ and the canonical global site comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-global-cohomology], these are the same morphism. Here ordinary sections and cohomology are [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]; the etale section map is $R\Gamma(X,\eta^e_L)$ followed by the canonical Leray identification $R\Gamma(X,rlL)\cong R\Gamma(Y,lL)$. Consequently the induced $H^q$ maps are the usual pullbacks for every $q\in\mathbf Z$, including zero groups in negative degrees. All displayed identifications are natural in the sheaf $L$.

proof.text: In the existing fixed-scalar module-sheaf model, define normalized derived base change by removing its identity target functor. Its defining factorization on homotopy complexes determines it uniquely. Compare these factorizations to prove compatibility with natural transformations, composition of exact source functors and source natural isomorphisms. For an exact left adjoint, its normalized derived unit is the actual derived adjunction unit. Combining this with the derived composition isomorphism gives the stated unit/Leray identity on each site. The right adjoints preserve injectives because their left adjoints are exact.

source.place: Step 4, transport; fixed-scalar adjunction and right-derived-functor expansion by Q9.

proof.text: For the underived comparison square, apply the conjugate-equivalence unit equation to the composite adjunctions. Evaluate at the identity object of the etale site. The changes of terminal object in the section functors are given by the unique terminal arrows, as follows from uniqueness of right adjoints to the constant-sheaf functor. Naturality of the inverse pullback comparison, followed by uniqueness of terminal arrows, gives the square of ordinary section units. Apply normalized derived composition and natural-isomorphism compatibility from the preceding step. Substituting finiteComparisonGlobalSections and fixedComparisonPullbackPlus yields the stated derived comparison square.

source.place: Step 4, transport; fixed-scalar adjunction and right-derived-functor expansion by Q9.

proof.text: If the etale unit is invertible, all factors of the proved unit equation are invertible: the comparison mate is invertible for finite coefficients and qcqs f. Hence the pro-etale unit is invertible. Each unit/Leray identity then expresses ordinary section pullback as a functor applied to an isomorphism followed by the Leray isomorphism, so both section maps are invertible.

source.place: Step 4, transport; fixed-scalar adjunction and right-derived-functor expansion by Q9.

proof.text: A sheaf placed in degree zero is in D^{>=0}. An exact functor preserves this bound, by its homology comparison isomorphism and preservation of zero objects. Apply this to etale pullback, comparison pullback and pro-etale pullback. Right-derived global sections of each resulting bounded-below complex have zero homology in negative degrees by the general right-derived lower-bound theorem. All identities are identities of natural transformations before specialization to L.
